headline: Graph and latent models predict cancer survival and drug response from incomplete omics
label: Oncology Multi Omic Outcome Prediction
summary: New TCGA-based methods address missing modalities, single-omic inputs, bulk deconvolution and cell-line-to-tumour transfer for oncology endpoints.
synthesis: The dominant thread is predicting oncology endpoints, mainly survival, drug response and subtype, when molecular input is partial, single-layer or inferred. DMG-PoE handles modality incompleteness with a dynamic modality graph and uncertainty-aware product-of-experts fusion. CMVAE instead uses contrastive survival alignment to strengthen a single-omic breast cancer latent space. DeSCENT adds reference-informed cellular profiles deconvolved from bulk RNA-seq to TCGA survival models. GOTSurv applies unbalanced optimal transport to cross-sectional survival data to derive risk strata and individual progression routes. For drug response, MODAE+ transfers cell-line pharmacogenomics to TCGA tumours through multi-objective domain adaptation with survival and lineage objectives. MulDR preserves omics-specific cell-line relations, and MTDKF predicts miRNA-drug-disease resistance and sensitivity triplets. HHRM classifies pan-cancer subtypes across up to eight hierarchy levels using SHAP attribution. A secondary strand covers single-cell perturbation response modeling: CytoWave pretraining, SPEAR's spectral flow model and RAPTORGraph's causal pathway beta-VAE.
